world.title: Israeli minister seeks citizenship revocation for Gaza filmmakers
world.summary: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar said he would immediately seek to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after their documentary NAZA won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday, Sept. 12. Zohar called the film “vile” and accused its creators of treason, saying the
world.content: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar said he would immediately seek to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after their documentary NAZA won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday, Sept. 12. Zohar called the film “vile” and accused its creators of treason, saying they were harming Israel to win applause from antisemites. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir also attacked the filmmakers and told them to leave Israel. The 80-minute documentary, produced with Guardian journalists, features anonymous testimony from 24 Israeli military and intelligence sources about surveillance, target selection and alleged AI-assisted attacks in Gaza. Its title refers to an Israeli military acronym for the estimated number of civilians expected to die in an airstrike. Israel rejects the film’s allegations and has criticized its use of anonymous sources. Abraham and Szor previously co-directed No Other Land, which won the 2025 Oscar for best documentary feature.

world.title: Trump downplays alleged Chinese intelligence aid before Iran strike
world.summary: President Trump on Sept. 13 downplayed a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities supplied Iran with high-resolution satellite imagery of Jordan’s Muwaffaq Salti Air Base before and after an Iranian missile strike on July 17. The attack killed three U.S. Army soldiers at the base, which hosts American forces. U
world.content: President Trump on Sept. 13 downplayed a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities supplied Iran with high-resolution satellite imagery of Jordan’s Muwaffaq Salti Air Base before and after an Iranian missile strike on July 17. The attack killed three U.S. Army soldiers at the base, which hosts American forces. U.S. officials cited by the Journal did not identify the Chinese entities or allege direct Chinese government involvement. Reuters said it could not immediately verify the report. Asked whether he would raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Trump did not answer directly and compared Chinese and U.S. intelligence activities. He said he still viewed relations with Xi positively. The two leaders are expected to meet at the White House on Sept. 24, although Beijing has not officially confirmed the meeting.

world.title: Indonesia intensifies search for 129 missing ferry passengers
world.summary: Indonesian authorities intensified the search on Monday for 129 people missing after the Virgo Transport 8 ferry overturned in rough seas in the Java Sea. The vessel was carrying 243 people — 213 passengers and 30 crew members — from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it lost contact early Su
world.content: Indonesian authorities intensified the search on Monday for 129 people missing after the Virgo Transport 8 ferry overturned in rough seas in the Java Sea. The vessel was carrying 243 people — 213 passengers and 30 crew members — from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it lost contact early Sunday. By Monday, six people had died and 108 had been rescued. Authorities deployed hundreds of rescuers and later found the overturned vessel about 148 kilometres from Banjarmasin. The cause remained under investigation.

world.title: Turkey launches nationwide LGBTQ raids, detaining dozens
world.summary: Turkish authorities carried out coordinated raids on LGBTQ+ associations, activists’ homes, bars and other venues in 15 provinces on Sept. 13, detaining at least 47 people, according to prosecutors and other reports. Al Jazeera, citing AFP, reported at least 63 detentions, while Kaos GL said nearly 50 activists were de
world.content: Turkish authorities carried out coordinated raids on LGBTQ+ associations, activists’ homes, bars and other venues in 15 provinces on Sept. 13, detaining at least 47 people, according to prosecutors and other reports. Al Jazeera, citing AFP, reported at least 63 detentions, while Kaos GL said nearly 50 activists were detained; the differing totals reflect separate provincial investigations and competing accounts. Authorities said prosecutors opened proceedings involving 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses, and seized drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a firearm. Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said the operation, named “My Family is Safe,” was part of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s “Decade of Family and Population” initiative. Prosecutors cited allegations including prostitution, obscenity, drug possession and the inappropriate influence of minors on sexual orientation and gender identity. Kaos GL and Turkish rights groups rejected the operation’s framing as state discrimination and said authorities had blocked dozens of websites and social-media accounts linked to LGBTQ+ organizations, activists and rights advocates.
world.image_alt: Turkey launches nationwide LGBTQ raids, detaining dozens

world.title: Canada seeks EU alliance as US trade ties worsen
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique alliance” with the European Union rather than seek membership, addressing reports that Ottawa was exploring an unprecedented “associate member” status. Carney said discussions would build on shared values, priorities and complementary strengths, whil
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique alliance” with the European Union rather than seek membership, addressing reports that Ottawa was exploring an unprecedented “associate member” status. Carney said discussions would build on shared values, priorities and complementary strengths, while Canadian officials told The Globe and Mail it was premature to give the relationship an official label. The proposed cooperation could cover freer movement of selected goods, services and workers in energy, artificial intelligence, defence and critical minerals, as well as underwater cables, data centres, cloud storage, satellite networks and infrastructure for shipping Canadian energy to Europe. Canada’s move follows an escalating trade dispute with the United States, including tariffs on tens of billions of dollars in cross-border commerce. President Trump has also said he intends to impose new tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and auto parts from January 1.

world.title: President Trump rejects AI slowdown over China race
world.summary: President Trump rejected calls to slow the development of advanced artificial intelligence, saying the United States must preserve its lead over China. Speaking to reporters at his golf resort in Doonbeg, Ireland, on Sept. 13, Trump said some safeguards could be added but dismissed warnings of catastrophic scenarios as
world.content: President Trump rejected calls to slow the development of advanced artificial intelligence, saying the United States must preserve its lead over China. Speaking to reporters at his golf resort in Doonbeg, Ireland, on Sept. 13, Trump said some safeguards could be added but dismissed warnings of catastrophic scenarios as claims by “negative forces” about events that would not happen. He gave no details of possible regulations. Amodei proposed pacing frontier-AI development so safety measures could catch up. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and xAI owner Elon Musk backed his call, while House Speaker Mike Johnson warned that emergency regulation or a moratorium could allow China to overtake the United States. Altman separately said OpenAI would not go public this year because of safety concerns.

world.title: Houthis seize Red Sea coast, pressure Saudi Arabia
world.summary: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement has expanded along the country’s Red Sea coast, capturing the port city of Mokha and Mayun Island, also known as Perim, at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The group also reported advances toward the Saudi-backed government strongholds of Taiz and Marib, while Yemeni governmen
world.content: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement has expanded along the country’s Red Sea coast, capturing the port city of Mokha and Mayun Island, also known as Perim, at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The group also reported advances toward the Saudi-backed government strongholds of Taiz and Marib, while Yemeni government forces attacked Houthi positions and pledged to send more troops to the coast. The Houthis claimed new missile and drone attacks on southern Saudi Arabia, including an alleged strike on a military base in Sharurah. Saudi authorities said a projectile struck the al-Tawwal area near the Yemeni border, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and other buildings. The United Nations estimated that more than 80,000 people had been displaced within Yemen since the beginning of September as renewed fighting threatened to reopen the country’s civil war.

world.title: Oman postpones Iran-Gulf talks on Strait of Hormuz
world.summary: Oman postponed talks between Iran, Iraq and Gulf states scheduled for Sept. 14 in Salalah on arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said Oman delayed the meeting “in the interests of consensus,” while an Iranian Foreign Ministry official said some regional countrie
world.content: Oman postponed talks between Iran, Iraq and Gulf states scheduled for Sept. 14 in Salalah on arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said Oman delayed the meeting “in the interests of consensus,” while an Iranian Foreign Ministry official said some regional countries had requested a postponement and that Tehran and Muscat jointly agreed to it. No new date was announced. Iran and Oman had been preparing a framework for temporary shipping routes through the strait, but participation by regional governments remained uncertain. Bahrain had ruled out attending, and other Gulf governments had not formally confirmed their participation. The postponement followed an attack on a commercial vessel in the strait that killed one person and a Houthi attack that damaged Saudi Arabia’s 1,200-kilometre east-west oil pipeline. The attacks increased concern over energy shipments and pushed oil prices higher when markets reopened.
world.image_alt: Oman postpones Iran-Gulf talks on Strait of Hormuz

business.title: Trump pressures Fed as Warsh faces rate-hike decision
business.summary: President Trump renewed his demand for lower U.S. interest rates on Sept. 13, saying the country should have the world’s lowest borrowing costs regardless of Federal Reserve data. He spoke to reporters in Doonbeg, Ireland, days before the Fed’s Sept. 15-16 policy meeting, where investors are pricing an 86% probability
business.content: President Trump renewed his demand for lower U.S. interest rates on Sept. 13, saying the country should have the world’s lowest borrowing costs regardless of Federal Reserve data. He spoke to reporters in Doonbeg, Ireland, days before the Fed’s Sept. 15-16 policy meeting, where investors are pricing an 86% probability of a rate increase. Trump’s demand conflicts with inflation data pointing toward tighter policy. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, whom Trump appointed and praised at a May swearing-in ceremony, faces that decision as August consumer prices rose 3.4% from a year earlier and core prices increased 2.4%. Energy costs and U.S. tariffs are adding to inflation risks. Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan expect a September hike, which some reports describe as the Fed’s first increase in about three years.

business.title: Anthropic selects Nasdaq for potential IPO at $2 trillion valuation
business.summary: Anthropic has selected Nasdaq for a potential initial public offering that could come as soon as October, according to a person familiar with the plans cited by Business Insider and Reuters. The Claude developer has filed preliminary IPO paperwork, but the share price, number of shares and final timetable remain unsett
business.content: Anthropic has selected Nasdaq for a potential initial public offering that could come as soon as October, according to a person familiar with the plans cited by Business Insider and Reuters. The Claude developer has filed preliminary IPO paperwork, but the share price, number of shares and final timetable remain unsettled, pending market conditions and regulatory review. Anthropic is considering raising as much as $100 billion at a valuation of about $2 trillion, although neither figure has been finalized. Nvidia is discussing an investment of up to $10 billion as a potential anchor investor, and Anthropic is also meeting with prospective investors, according to people familiar with the discussions, which could change. CEO Dario Amodei is seeking to slow the pace of AI development while the company prepares for the listing, CNBC reported.

business.title: UK prime minister urges culture shift to support businesses
business.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell business leaders that the UK needs a “culture shift” to make it easier to start and grow companies when he meets senior executives at 10 Downing Street on Monday, September 14. He said entrepreneurs who take risks should receive backing from government and that local leaders should
business.content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell business leaders that the UK needs a “culture shift” to make it easier to start and grow companies when he meets senior executives at 10 Downing Street on Monday, September 14. He said entrepreneurs who take risks should receive backing from government and that local leaders should have more power to work with companies. Burnham is expected to describe the government as a “partner for growth” and promise support for strong business ideas. The meeting includes executives from BP, Shell, HSBC, Morrisons, Sainsbury’s, BT, Vodafone and Rolls-Royce, while Chancellor John Healey prepares his first Budget next month. The government faces criticism over higher business costs after employer national insurance and minimum-wage changes introduced under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer, while rising borrowing costs are increasing pressure on public finances.

business.title: Amazon pauses cargo operations with 21 Air after Miami crash
business.summary: Amazon said Sept. 13 that it had paused operations with Miami-based cargo carrier 21 Air, which operated Flight 7598 for Amazon Air. The decision followed a Sept. 6 runway overrun at Miami International Airport, when a Boeing 767-300 struck vehicles outside the runway; five people on the ground died and five others wer
business.content: Amazon said Sept. 13 that it had paused operations with Miami-based cargo carrier 21 Air, which operated Flight 7598 for Amazon Air. The decision followed a Sept. 6 runway overrun at Miami International Airport, when a Boeing 767-300 struck vehicles outside the runway; five people on the ground died and five others were injured. Amazon said it supported the investigation and reviewed the circumstances surrounding the crash before suspending the partnership. The National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation. Amazon said it would continue supporting the investigation and those affected; 21 Air said it was cooperating with authorities and remained confident in its safety policies, procedures and training.

business.content: Michael Dell’s family office, DFO Management, is nearing a deal with Sequence to acquire The Baldwin Insurance Group and take the insurance broker private in a transaction valued at about $7.7 billion, the Financial Times reported. Baldwin had a market value of about $4.2 billion, according to Bloomberg’s account of the report. The reports did not provide details on financing, the proposed premium, regulatory approvals or a closing timetable.

business.title: Saudi pipeline shutdown pushes oil above $107 a barrel
business.summary: Oil prices rose Sept. 14 after Saudi Arabia suspended its East-West pipeline following drone attacks. The pipeline had carried about 4 million barrels per day to the Red Sea, bypassing the disrupted Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose 2.8% to $107.54 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate gained 2.3% to $102.34, extending
business.content: Oil prices rose Sept. 14 after Saudi Arabia suspended its East-West pipeline following drone attacks. The pipeline had carried about 4 million barrels per day to the Red Sea, bypassing the disrupted Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose 2.8% to $107.54 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate gained 2.3% to $102.34, extending gains from the previous week, when both benchmarks rose above $100. Saudi Arabia said the drones originated from Iraqi territory, while Iraq condemned the attack and ordered an investigation; no group has claimed responsibility. Renewed attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi seizure of Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb have also affected routes used for oil and commercial traffic. Traders and Saudi oil buyers said stocks at Yanbu could sustain exports for only five to seven days; repair estimates ranged from a quick partial restart to five or six weeks. Oman’s foreign minister said a planned meeting between Iran and Gulf states on passage through Hormuz had been postponed.
business.image_alt: Saudi pipeline shutdown pushes oil above $107 a barrel

business.title: Anthropic signals second consecutive profitable quarter ahead of planned IPO
business.summary: Anthropic has told a small group of shareholders that it expects positive adjusted operating income for a second consecutive quarter, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The Claude developer is presenting the forecast as it prepares for a planned initial public offering and faces
business.content: Anthropic has told a small group of shareholders that it expects positive adjusted operating income for a second consecutive quarter, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The Claude developer is presenting the forecast as it prepares for a planned initial public offering and faces investor scrutiny over the cash requirements of frontier-AI development. The adjusted measure excludes costs such as stock-based compensation. Anthropic’s gross margin exceeded 80% before revenue-sharing payments to distribution partners such as Amazon and model-training costs, according to two people familiar with the figures. Reports said the company selected Nasdaq for a listing that could value it at $2 trillion or more. Anthropic declined to comment.

business.title: Lawmakers revisit Social Security tax hikes before 2032
business.summary: A growing group of U.S. lawmakers, including some Republicans, is considering ways to raise Social Security revenue as the program’s trust fund approaches insolvency. Projections cited in the reporting indicate that benefits could be reduced by 22% by 2032 unless Congress changes the program’s finances. Social Security
business.content: A growing group of U.S. lawmakers, including some Republicans, is considering ways to raise Social Security revenue as the program’s trust fund approaches insolvency. Projections cited in the reporting indicate that benefits could be reduced by 22% by 2032 unless Congress changes the program’s finances. Social Security relies on payroll taxes paid by workers and employers, but those taxes no longer generate enough revenue to fund current benefits. Lawmakers have discussed raising the tax rate, increasing the amount of income subject to the tax or taking other steps to increase revenue after years of congressional inaction on benefit cuts and tax increases.

science.title: Astronomers unmask a supernova impostor
science.summary: Astronomers studying a distant star that has produced explosive outbursts for about a decade say new research challenges the view that it is nearing a supernova. The findings instead suggest that a previously unseen companion star may be responsible for the behavior. Separate research using gravitational-wave data is h
science.content: Astronomers studying a distant star that has produced explosive outbursts for about a decade say new research challenges the view that it is nearing a supernova. The findings instead suggest that a previously unseen companion star may be responsible for the behavior. Separate research using gravitational-wave data is helping determine whether an unusual merger involved an exotic compact object rather than two black holes. Researchers say mergers between black holes can generate spacetime ripples resembling signals from other compact-object mergers, complicating efforts to identify the objects involved.

science.title: Strong El Niño raises global weather risks through 2027
science.summary: A strengthening El Niño is expected to become very strong during Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter. U.S. forecasters put the chance of strong conditions above 90% and the chance of an event stronger than every El Niño since 1950 at 75%. In the central Pacific, three-month sea-surface temperatures would need to aver
science.content: A strengthening El Niño is expected to become very strong during Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter. U.S. forecasters put the chance of strong conditions above 90% and the chance of an event stronger than every El Niño since 1950 at 75%. In the central Pacific, three-month sea-surface temperatures would need to average more than 4.5 degrees Fahrenheit (2.5 degrees Celsius) above normal to meet that threshold. August’s average was slightly above 3 degrees, and temperatures are forecast to rise through at least November. The pattern is already associated with regional weather differences. The Atlantic recorded five named storms but no hurricanes by Sept. 13, setting a satellite-era record for the latest date without an Atlantic hurricane; the previous record was Sept. 11 in 2002 and 2013. California has a higher likelihood of a wetter-than-normal winter, while the UAE and Gulf could face heavier rainfall and greater flooding risks, mainly in October-November and March-May. Vietnam’s Mekong Delta is preparing for an earlier end to the rainy season, drought, saltwater intrusion and dry-season water shortages.
science.image_alt: Strong El Niño raises global weather risks through 2027

science.title: SpaceX launches O3b mPOWER trio on 700th Falcon mission
science.summary: SpaceX launched three telecommunications satellites for SES on Sept. 13, completing deployment of the O3b mPOWER constellation and marking the 700th Falcon rocket launch. A Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 2:49 p.m. EDT (1849 UTC). The O3b mPOWER-F mis
science.content: SpaceX launched three telecommunications satellites for SES on Sept. 13, completing deployment of the O3b mPOWER constellation and marking the 700th Falcon rocket launch. A Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 2:49 p.m. EDT (1849 UTC). The O3b mPOWER-F mission carried satellites F11, F12 and F13 to medium Earth orbit. Boeing built the spacecraft. SES is SpaceX’s oldest commercial customer.

science.title: AI tools assist nanoscale microscopy and automate membrane mapping
science.summary: Researchers reported two AI systems for microscopy-related workflows. Scientists at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory created a framework that enables atomic force microscopes to identify important nanoscale features and autonomously direct closer examination to the most informative areas of
science.content: Researchers reported two AI systems for microscopy-related workflows. Scientists at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory created a framework that enables atomic force microscopes to identify important nanoscale features and autonomously direct closer examination to the most informative areas of a sample. A separate team from Helmholtz Munich, the Technical University of Munich and the University of Basel developed MemBrain v2 to automate three-dimensional mapping of cell membranes and their proteins. According to the Nature Methods study, the tool reduced analysis time from weeks to hours and produced results that matched manual analysis.

science.title: Himalayan glacier melt accelerates as monitoring gaps widen
science.summary: A report by Systemiq, the Integrated Mountain Initiative, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development and India’s G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment says Himalayan glaciers are losing mass 65% faster than they did a decade ago, threatening water security as the Himalaya–Karakoram reg
science.content: A report by Systemiq, the Integrated Mountain Initiative, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development and India’s G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment says Himalayan glaciers are losing mass 65% faster than they did a decade ago, threatening water security as the Himalaya–Karakoram region approaches “peak water” by mid-century. The report says retreating glaciers are leaving behind expanding lakes held back by unstable rock and ice, while warming is destabilising permafrost and high-mountain slopes, increasing the risk of cascading hazards. Only about 21 of an estimated 40,000 glaciers in the Himalaya–Karakoram region receive detailed, sustained monitoring, the report says. The findings follow deadly flooding and landslides in Nepal and Tibet after a late-August glacier collapse; cited coverage reported more than 1,300 people dead and more than 5,300 missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet region. India’s government has classified 56 glacial lakes as “very high risk,” while the Himalayan region accounts for about 35% of India’s disasters despite covering about 18% of its land area.
science.image_alt: Himalayan glacier melt accelerates as monitoring gaps widen

science.title: US science cuts drive young researchers toward overseas careers
science.summary: A survey of early-career U.S. researchers found that federal science funding cuts and grant freezes introduced in 2025 created severe professional and mental distress. Sixty percent of respondents said they were considering moving abroad, while 56.7% said they were considering leaving academic research altogether. The
science.content: A survey of early-career U.S. researchers found that federal science funding cuts and grant freezes introduced in 2025 created severe professional and mental distress. Sixty percent of respondents said they were considering moving abroad, while 56.7% said they were considering leaving academic research altogether. The affected group includes undergraduate researchers, doctoral candidates and postdoctoral fellows, whose stipends and positions often depend directly on federal grants. The disruptions followed rapid policy changes by the Trump administration, including proposed double-digit reductions to federal science budgets, freezes or terminations of hundreds of existing grants, and pauses to some diversity and climate programs. Universities subsequently began shrinking graduate-student support.
science.image_alt: US science cuts drive young researchers toward overseas careers

science.title: Fall 2026 skywatching guide highlights planets and meteor showers
science.summary: A fall 2026 skywatching guide identifies the Andromeda Galaxy, the Pleiades star cluster and the season’s first supermoon among prominent celestial sights visible in September, October and November. The guide also lists distant planets reaching opposition, several meteor showers and opportunities to photograph galaxies
science.content: A fall 2026 skywatching guide identifies the Andromeda Galaxy, the Pleiades star cluster and the season’s first supermoon among prominent celestial sights visible in September, October and November. The guide also lists distant planets reaching opposition, several meteor showers and opportunities to photograph galaxies and nebulae with smart telescopes. Longer nights provide more time for observation, and many of the listed sights are visible without specialist equipment; some are best viewed with the naked eye. November will bring the season’s first full supermoon.
science.image_alt: Fall 2026 skywatching guide highlights planets and meteor showers

science.title: AI leaders debate slowdown after extinction warnings
science.summary: A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher, Jacob Coxon, warned that leading AI companies are racing toward self-improving superintelligence without adequate safeguards. Coxon said continuing at the current pace could create a substantial chance of human extinction in the near future. His warning followed his resignation
science.content: A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher, Jacob Coxon, warned that leading AI companies are racing toward self-improving superintelligence without adequate safeguards. Coxon said continuing at the current pace could create a substantial chance of human extinction in the near future. His warning followed his resignation from Anthropic and a widely circulated post dated Sept. 9. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for slower frontier-model development, arguing that safety work needs time to catch up with capability gains. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI CEO Elon Musk have publicly supported an industry-wide slowdown, regulation and independent monitoring, while critics have questioned whether existential warnings also serve companies’ commercial interests. Amodei separately warned that a swarm of AI agents could take over the internet within six to 12 months without stronger safeguards.
science.image_alt: AI leaders debate slowdown after extinction warnings

sports.title: Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 to reach League Cup semi-finals
sports.summary: Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 at Ibrox on September 13 to reach the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals, giving Derek McInnes his first Old Firm victory as Rangers manager. Captain Dan Neil scored in the 23rd and 75th minutes, either side of Kevin Kelsy’s 59th-minute goal, as Rangers controlled the match physically and tactically
sports.content: Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 at Ibrox on September 13 to reach the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals, giving Derek McInnes his first Old Firm victory as Rangers manager. Captain Dan Neil scored in the 23rd and 75th minutes, either side of Kevin Kelsy’s 59th-minute goal, as Rangers controlled the match physically and tactically. The result ended Celtic’s League Cup campaign and extended Rangers’ winning streak to five matches in all competitions following their European qualifying campaign.
sports.image_alt: Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 to reach League Cup semi-finals

sports.title: Shane Lowry sets Irish Open record with 11-shot win
sports.summary: Shane Lowry won the Amgen Irish Open by a record 11 shots at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare, on Sunday, finishing at 23-under par after a final-round 63. The 39-year-old Irishman made eight birdies and one bogey, sealing the victory with a birdie on the 18th hole before a home crowd and Preside
sports.content: Shane Lowry won the Amgen Irish Open by a record 11 shots at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare, on Sunday, finishing at 23-under par after a final-round 63. The 39-year-old Irishman made eight birdies and one bogey, sealing the victory with a birdie on the 18th hole before a home crowd and President Trump, who presented the trophy. The title was Lowry’s second Irish Open victory, 17 years after he won the event as an amateur, and his first individual tournament win since the 2022 BMW PGA Championship. His 23-under total was seven shots better than Jon Rahm’s previous 72-hole tournament record, while Patrick Reed and Joaquin Niemann shared second place at 12-under.
sports.image_alt: Shane Lowry sets Irish Open record with 11-shot win

sports.title: Clippers owner Ballmer accepts NBA sanctions, drops legal challenge
sports.summary: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer said Sunday that he and the franchise will comply with the NBA’s sanctions for salary-cap circumvention and will not pursue legal action. The league suspended Ballmer for one year, fined the Clippers $30 million and ordered the team to forfeit five first-round draft picks. Ballm
sports.content: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer said Sunday that he and the franchise will comply with the NBA’s sanctions for salary-cap circumvention and will not pursue legal action. The league suspended Ballmer for one year, fined the Clippers $30 million and ordered the team to forfeit five first-round draft picks. Ballmer said the fine has been paid. Ballmer apologized to Clippers fans, employees and fellow NBA owners while maintaining that he disputes some of the league’s findings. The NBA’s nearly yearlong investigation by an outside firm examined arrangements involving Kawhi Leonard and team sponsors or business partners. The Clippers had initially called the investigation biased and said they would challenge the ruling.
sports.image_alt: Clippers owner Ballmer accepts NBA sanctions, drops legal challenge

sports.title: Brighton rout 10-man Coventry 5-0 in Premier League
sports.summary: Brighton & Hove Albion beat newly promoted Coventry City 5-0 at the Coventry Building Society Arena on Sunday to move into fourth place in the Premier League with seven points from four matches. Charalampos Kostoulas opened the scoring, Malick Yalcouyé added a second, and Pascal Groß converted a penalty before Lewis Du
sports.content: Brighton & Hove Albion beat newly promoted Coventry City 5-0 at the Coventry Building Society Arena on Sunday to move into fourth place in the Premier League with seven points from four matches. Charalampos Kostoulas opened the scoring, Malick Yalcouyé added a second, and Pascal Groß converted a penalty before Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari completed the rout. Coventry played most of the second half with 10 men after Taiwo Awoniyi received a straight red card for elbowing Maxim De Cuyper. The result left Frank Lampard’s side bottom of the table after a fourth successive defeat without scoring, as the only team yet to claim a league point.
sports.image_alt: Brighton rout 10-man Coventry 5-0 in Premier League

sports.content: Harry Kane scored in the 72nd minute to give defending champions Bayern Munich a 2-1 victory over promoted Elversberg in the Bundesliga on September 13. Lennart Karl put Bayern ahead in the 26th minute, but Maurice Krattenmacher equalized with a curling shot shortly after the hour before Kane restored the lead. The result lifted Bayern to seven points after three matches and ended Elversberg’s perfect start to its first Bundesliga campaign. The goal was Kane’s first league strike of the season and his 150th for Bayern in 153 appearances in all competitions. It also took him to 99 Bundesliga goals in 97 matches, one short of Dieter Müller’s record for the fastest 100 Bundesliga goals, achieved in 129 appearances.

sports.content: Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix at Madrid’s new Madring circuit on September 13, beating Max Verstappen by 4.351 seconds and Lando Norris by 5.089 seconds. The 20-year-old claimed his eighth victory in 14 races and extended his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 81 points, with 292 points to Russell’s 211. Norris started from pole and led until a virtual safety car was triggered on lap 15 after Lance Stroll stopped his Aston Martin. Norris had already passed the pit entry, allowing Antonelli and Verstappen to pit under the reduced-speed conditions. Norris stopped a lap later, had a seven-second service and dropped to fifth before recovering to third. Charles Leclerc finished fourth after leading much of the race before making his mandatory stop, while Russell was fifth and Lewis Hamilton retired on lap seven with brake failure.

sports.content: Europe defeated the United States 15-13 at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands on Sunday to reclaim the Solheim Cup after the teams were tied 8-8 through the opening two days. Europe won the final-day singles 7-5, with Charley Hull opening the charge by beating Megan Khang 3&2 and Lottie Woad defeating Auston Kim 2&1 to help Europe reach the 14-point mark. Carlota Ciganda sealed the result with a 4&2 win over Jennifer Kupcho, taking Europe to 15 points, above the 14½ required under the competition format. The victory gave Anna Nordqvist a Solheim Cup title in her first campaign as Europe’s captain. Hull and Woad rebounded from losing three of four matches together over the first two days by winning their decisive singles matches.

sports.content: The Chicago Bears opened the 2026 NFL season with a 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte on September 13. The teams combined for 96 points, the highest total in a season opener in league history. The total surpassed the previous record of 88, set when Tampa Bay defeated New Orleans 48-40 in 2018. Chicago also broke its franchise record for points in an opener, set in 1948, while the Panthers allowed the most points in team history. Caleb Williams accounted for four touchdowns, throwing for 269 yards and two scores while rushing for 65 yards and two touchdowns. D’Andre Swift ran for 124 yards and three touchdowns on 18 carries, and rookie Kyle Monangai added 100 rushing yards, including a 61-yard touchdown. Chicago totaled 552 yards, including 291 on the ground, and forced three turnovers. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns.
